title: Plants, Animals and Habitats
seo_title: Primary 2 Basic Science: Plants, Animals and Habitats Worksheets (NERDC)
standard_code: Primary 2 Basic Science: Living and Non-Living Things
standard_text: Plants and animals live in habitats that meet their needs for food, water, shelter and space; their body parts help them survive in their habitats. (summary of the Basic Science curriculum, Primary 2, theme: Living and Non-Living Things)
meta_desc: Free Primary 2 Basic Science worksheets (NERDC curriculum, theme: Living and Non-Living Things): what plants need, growing plants, habitats, animal needs and shelters and suited to a habitat. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Plants need light, water, air and nutrients.
key_sub: A habitat gives food, water and shelter.
body_html:
How to think about it

Green plants need sunlight, water, air (carbon dioxide) and nutrients from the soil to grow well. A plant kept in the dark grows pale and weak; a plant without water wilts.

A habitat is where a plant or animal lives. It gives food, water, shelter and a place to raise young. Animals build shelters such as weaver nests, termite mounds, burrows and spider webs. Living things have features that suit their habitat.

Example

A bush baby is active at night and has very big eyes. How do its eyes help it?

Night habitat

Answer: they help it see in the dark

Example

Which habitat suits a mudskipper?

Muddy shore with tides

Answer: a mangrove swamp

Common mistakes

  • Thinking plants get their food from the soil.
  • Thinking a habitat is only a house built by people.
  • Forgetting that plants need air.

faq.q: Why does a weaver bird build its nest at the end of a branch?
faq.a: Snakes and other predators find it hard to reach.

faq.q: Can two animals share a habitat?
faq.a: Yes. A habitat is home to many kinds of plants and animals.

items.q: Which feature would most help a living thing survive in a hot, dry desert?
items.e: Features fit the conditions of the habitat.

items.q: A millipede curls up when it is touched. How does this help it survive?
c: It helps it protect itself from predators.
It helps it stay in damp soil and avoid drying out.
It helps it get sunlight at the surface of the pond.
It helps it catch insects for food.
items.e: This adaptation helps the millipede protect itself from predators.

items.q: A banksia has hard, woody seed pods. How does this feature help it survive?
c: to hop long distances to find food and water

to reflect sunlight and lose less water
to detect small animals in muddy water
items.e: This is a structural adaptation: a body part that helps the banksia survive.

items.q: Which of these is a structural adaptation?

a spider that spins a web
items.e: Structural adaptations are body parts. Behavioural adaptations are things an organism does.

items.q: Which feature would most help a living thing survive in a muddy, salty shore?

items.e: Structural adaptations are body parts. Behavioural adaptations are things an organism does.

items.q: A cactus has spines instead of leaves. How does this help it survive?

items.q: A eucalyptus has thick, waxy leaves that hang down. How does this feature help it survive?

items.q: A mangrove tree has breathing roots that stick up out of the mud. How does this help it survive?

items.e: This adaptation helps the mangrove tree take in air from above the waterlogged mud.

items.q: How do the woody pods of banksias help them survive bushfires?
c: The pods protect seeds and open after a fire.
They make the tree grow faster.
items.e: New plants grow after the fire.
